description: Phase 2 evidence: the Sylf character as composable pixel content, verified against the real development surface.

model.authoredAsPixelData: reference-grid spans resolved to a palette at draw time; no image, SVG, sprite sheet or texture

liveChecks.method: Read from the real dev surface in a browser, not from jsdom.
liveChecks.conclusion: Suppressing a plane removes its cells and nothing else — the body and leaves are byte-identical throughout.

engineBoundaryTypecheck.note: The engine is still DOM-free after content was rewritten.

defectsFoundAndFixed: The state composition table gated nothing: render painted every plane, so IDLE drew blush. All painting now routes through selectsPlane.
focused was geometrically identical to open, so FOCUSING was indistinguishable from IDLE. Every eye shape now occupies distinct cells, enforced by test.
Plane hiding was a post-render patch that the next full composite immediately undid. Suppression is now content state, so it survives repeated frames.
A sparkle sat under the character hem, making the scenery-order assertion ambiguous; it moved.
The hem deep edge was painted past the row end, widening the silhouette by a column; it is now the last column of the shade run.
Shading used a fixed split, making the narrow crown rows almost all highlight; the split is now a share of each row width.

presentationCandidates.finding: Rendering the real character confirmed each Phase 0 candidate without invalidating any. At 32 the eye ink and glint merge and the face stops reading; at 48 both survive at dashboard-card size.

visualCaptures.shows: Character at a 456px preview, dark mode, with all Phase 2 review controls
The same character at a 108px dashboard-card slot, and the 32/40/48/64 resolution comparison
Body and leaves only, with eyes and blush suppressed — the figure is intact without its face

limits: Live high-DPI rendering remains unobserved (O13): neither environment could force a device pixel ratio above 1.
The 640px presentation slot is clamped to 464px by the dev layout, so sizes above that are asserted in tests rather than observed.
Visual correctness still rests on recorded captures plus human review; the deterministic tests do not prove it.
No production surface renders this character yet, so nothing here is evidence about a real dashboard card.
